verses.text: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.
On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.
This is the history of the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that Yahweh  God made the earth and the heavens.
No plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for Yahweh God had not caused it to rain on the earth. There was not a man to till the ground,
but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
Yahweh God planted a garden eastward, in Eden, and there he put the man whom he had formed.

Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food, including the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became the source of four rivers.
The name of the first is Pishon: it flows through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium  and onyx stone are also there.
The name of the second river is Gihon. It is the same river that flows through the whole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Hiddekel. This is the one which flows in front of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
Yahweh God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
Yahweh God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to  him.”

Out of the ground Yahweh God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
The man gave names to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for man there was not found a helper comparable to him.
Yahweh God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
Yahweh God made a woman from the rib which he had taken from the man, and brought her to the man.
The man said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘woman,’ because she was taken out of Man.”
Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
The man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.

footnotes.content: I look up from my work and see the heavens and earth complete, and I am reminded that our God is a finisher. He does not leave what He begins half-done, and that gives an old heart rest in the faithfulness of Jesus, who will also finish His work in us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It humbles me that the Almighty, who needs nothing, chose to rest. He was not weary in the sense we are, but He graciously marked a pattern for His creatures. How kind of Him to teach us that our worth is not in how much we produce, but in belonging to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God sets apart a day as holy, not to hoard it for Himself, but to bless us with it. I have learned that stopping to rest with the Lord is itself an act of trust. In a world that demands more, He invites us to cease and remember that the world is held together by Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses calls us back to remember: this is the history of the heavens and earth when Yahweh God made them. I love that He reveals Himself by name here as Yahweh God - the covenant-keeping One who made all things and who has always purposed to draw near to the ones He made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the rain fell, there was no man to till the ground - so the Lord was already planning to give man a place and a calling. I see grace here: God does not wait for us to prove useful before He cares for us. He first prepares the soil, then places us in it to tend what He has made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A gentle mist rose to water the whole ground - no thunderstorm, just tender provision. It reminds me that our God often cares for us in quiet ways we barely notice. I have learned to thank Him more for the mist than for the miracle, for both come from the same faithful hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What wonder: the God who spoke galaxies into being stoops down to form man from dust, and breathes life into him. I am made of humble earth, yet made to bear His breath. No wonder our hearts long for Him - we are only truly alive when we draw near to the One who first breathed us into being.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh God planted a garden and put the man there Himself - He delights to give His creature a place of delight. I picture an old gardener lovingly placing Adam where he would be cared for and cared for things. How like our Savior, who goes before us to prepare a place for us still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food was there, and right in the middle stood the tree of life. God gave abundantly before He gave a test. I have found that is always His way - He first fills our hands with mercy, then asks for our trust. May my heart feast on His gifts and long most for Him who is the true Tree of Life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A river flowed from Eden to water the garden and parted into four - Pishon through Havilah (with gold, bdellium, onyx), Gihon through Cush, Hiddekel before Assyria, and the Euphrates. These real place-names anchor Eden in a real geography God made, not a fable. I take comfort that the God who marked those rivers also knows the rivers and roads of my own life, and still waters the places He has planted me.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The man was not placed in the garden to be served, but to serve it - to cultivate and keep it. I have learned there is great dignity in tending what God has entrusted to us, whether it is a garden, a home, or a soul. Our labor in His world, offered in faith, is never wasted in the hands of our faithful Creator.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How generous the command is: 'You may freely eat of every tree of the garden.' Before a single 'no' comes an ocean of 'yes'. I find that is the heart of God with His children. He delights to give, and His boundaries are never stingy - they are guardrails to protect the joy He has freely given us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One tree, one boundary, and the warning is solemn: in the day you eat, you will surely die. I grieve that we so quickly trade the abundant yes for the one forbidden no. Yet I praise God that in Jesus, the true Man, we who deserved death have been given life - for He took our dying so that we might never taste the death our sin earned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It is the first time God says something is not good: 'It is not good for the man to be alone.' Even in a perfect garden, isolation was not His design for Adam. I am grateful that the God who made us also knows our need for relationship. And how much more grateful I am that in Jesus we are never alone - He has drawn near to us and calls us His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God brings the animals to Adam to name them, inviting him to exercise his God-given wisdom and stewardship. I smile to think of that moment - a man learning the world his Creator had made, naming each creature as it passed by. It reminds me that to know God's works is a joy, and to care for them is part of the image we bear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adam named them all, but none proved to be a helper comparable to him. I think God was gently showing Adam his need, not leaving him frustrated but preparing him to rejoice when the answer came. Our God is so kind - He often lets us feel our lack so that we will be all the more thankful when He meets it in His perfect way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam - tenderly putting him under, doing the work Himself while Adam could do nothing. I see a picture here of grace: the first bride was brought forth while the first man slept. It makes me think of our true Bridegroom, who went into the sleep of death to bring forth His bride, the church, for His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God did not snatch Eve into existence from nowhere - He took from Adam what was already his, and fashioned it into something beautiful for him. There is such care in this. The Lord takes what belongs to us and, in His grace, forms it into a gift we would never have dreamed of. He is always better to us than we know how to ask.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Adam bursts forth in joy: 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh!' After searching all creatures, at last he finds one like himself, yet wonderfully different. I think our first parents knew something of what every godly marriage has known since - the joy of being seen, known, and joined to one whom God Himself has brought.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this union: a man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife, and the two become one flesh. As of 2026-10, I am grateful that this God-given picture points beyond itself to the greater union - Christ the Bridegroom and His church, cleaved to one another by grace, never to be parted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Naked and unashamed - what a precious glimpse of how it was meant to be. No hiding, no fear, no shame, because there was no sin. I long for that day when, in Christ, all shame is fully taken away and we stand before our God clothed in His righteousness, naked no more and unashamed forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
